newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta banks report strong performance.
newsitem.headline: Malta banks report strong performance.

text.p: Malta's Mid-Med Bank and Bank of Valletta groups reported strong performance in the six months ending on March 31.
Mid-Med group, which includes an offshore subsidiary, said its profit rose by eight percent over the six months ending on March 31, 1996, to 7.3 million Malta pounds ($18.89 million).

The group's operating income rose to 17.21 million pounds from 15.27 million, of which net interest income this year reached 13.33 million pounds. Earnings per share were up to 13.2 cents from 9.7 cents in March 1996.
The Malta government has a 67 percent stake in Mid-Med, and Finance Minister Leo Brincat said on Friday the government had no intention of selling it.

Bank of Valletta privatised three years ago, said it made a pre-tax profit of 7.2 million pounds in the six months up to March 31, 1997, a record increase of 26.7 percent over the same period a year ago.

Net interest income increased by 16.3 percent to 12.2 million pounds and group assets climbed to 987.1 million, an increase of 72.5 million pounds (15.9 percent) from March 31, 1996. Customer deposits rose to 782.5 million from 719.9 million the previous year.
Shareholders' funds increased by 5.6 million (21.3 percent) to 58.1 million pounds.
The Bank of Valletta group includes an offshore subsidiary and an investment bank.
